entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Rahul Kumar Tripathi - Advocate for appellants.

Shri Nitin Gupta - Government
Advocate for State.

Heard on I.A. No.983/2021, which is first application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant No.1-Devendra
Vishwakarma.

Appellant No.1 is aggrieved of the judgment dated 16.01.2020 passed by learned Special Judge,
POCSO, District Tikamgarh in S.C. No.400013/2016, whereby the present appellant-Devendra Vishwakarma has been convicted for the offence under Section 376 (2) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act with 14 years R.I. and fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulation of three months R.I..
He has also been convicted for the offence under Sections 366 and 368 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years with fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulation of additional R.I. for 3 months.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent.
It is a case of consent.
The statement of prosecutrix under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. clearly reveals that she had gone on her own volition.
It is submitted that evidence of PW-8, father of prosecutrix creates doubt about the date of birth of prosecutrix.

He has admitted that he had not admitted the prosecutrix in the school though name of PW-8 is mentioned in the school entry register Ex.P/6.
2 CRA-992-2020 It is also submitted that though this witness has denied a suggestion that after taking money he enter into a compromise but fact of the matter is that now the prosecutrix is married and she is living her married life happily.
The appellant has been falsely implicated.
The appeal will take time for its conclusion.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant-Devendra Vishwakarma and to release him on bail.

Pleadings from the evidence of school teacher PW-4, it is pointed out that he has admitted in his cross examination that no documentary evidence was given at the time of recording of date of birth of the prosecutrix on Ex.P/6.

He has also admitted this suggestion that normally in rural setting children are admitted at the age of 7-8 years but their age is mentioned as 3-4 years with a view to take advantage in education and service.

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate for the State opposes the suspension application.

Taking all this facts into consideration and especially this fact that there is no documentary evidence like birth certificate etc. brought on record by the prosecution to prove the exact date of birth of the prosecutrix, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant - Devendra Vishwakarma and to release him on bail.
Accordingly, I.A.No.983/2021 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with 3 CRA-992-2020 two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 16/12/2024 and such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence imposed upon Appellant- Devendra Vishwakarma shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
Certified copy as per rules.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL) (VINA  JUDGE J  irfan Devendra Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182736755/
